item.research_question: What is the oxidation behavior of the refractory AlNbTiVZr 0.25 high-entropy alloy at temperatures between 600 and 900 °C?
item.material_system: AlNbTiVZr 0.25 (nominal composition: Al 25.0, Nb 22.4, Ti 24.0, V 21.9, Zr 6.7 at.%)
item.processing_route: Arc melting in low-pressure high-purity argon; homogenization at 1200 °C for 24 h; specimens cut via electric discharge machine and polished with colloidal silica suspension
item.test_conditions: Static lab air at 600, 700, and 800 °C for 100 h, and 900 °C for 50 h; mass measurements at intervals of 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100 h
key_findings: At 600–700 °C, two-stage oxidation kinetics were observed: nearly parabolic (n = 0.46–0.48) transitioning to breakaway (n = 0.75–0.72).
At 800 °C, oxidation kinetics were nearly linear (n = 0.92) throughout the entire duration.
At 900 °C, the specimen disintegrated after 50 h of testing.
Specific mass gains were 7.2, 38.1, and 107.5 mg/cm² at 600, 700, and 800 °C for 100 h, and 225.5 mg/cm² at 900 °C for 50 h.
The surface layer at 600 °C consisted of V₂O₅, VO₂, TiO₂, Nb₂O₅, and TiNb₂O₇ oxides.
The surface layer at 900 °C comprised complex TiNb₂O₇, AlNbO₄, and Nb₂Zr₆O₁₇ oxides.
At 600 °C, cracks nucleated at the scale-metal interface and propagated towards the surface, with oxide scale thickness varying from ~15 μm to ~30 μm.
At 800 °C, the oxide scale was significantly thicker (~800 μm) and porous, with whiskers of ~1.5 μm average transversal size.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the acceleration of oxidation at the second stage (600–700 °C) to breakaway oxidation caused by scale cracking/spallation due to the nucleation of voluminous Nb₂O₅ and TiNb₂O₇ oxides, and partial evaporation of V₂O₅ at 700 °C. At 800 °C, severe oxidation is driven by the evaporation of volatile V-rich oxides (particularly V₂O₅), which creates pores that serve as places for accelerated oxygen ingress, alongside the formation of unprotective complex oxides (TiNb₂O₇, AlNbO₄, Nb₂Zr₆O₁₇).
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes the alloy shows rather poor oxidation resistance which limits potential applications.
item.future_work: To improve oxidation resistance, modification of the chemical composition (reduction of V or Ti, addition of Al, Cr, or Si) or the use of protective coatings is required.
quotes: At 600–700 °C, two-stage oxidation kinetics was found: Nearly parabolic oxidation (n = 0.46–0.48) at the first stage, transitioned to breakaway oxidation (n = 0.75–0.72) at the second stage.
The main reason for severe oxidation were the pores, which served as places for accelerated ingress of oxygen toward the bare metal, and appeared as a result of the evaporation of V-rich oxides.
